doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Becoming a leader because junkie bandleaders did not pay
summary: Junkie leaders not paying him, including Buhaina, pushed him to lead his own band.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Before we paused, I was asking about the New York studio scene in the late ‘50s­ early ‘60s, and whether that had tempted you at all. You stated it was too confining. Where I want to go from that is, when did you know you wanted to be the leader of a group? You haven’t done a whole of sideman things for 55 years or so.

I knew I wanted to be a leader when I started working for guys that were junkies. Because they wouldn’t pay you. Rather than to beat them up, guys that I liked, I just said, “Well, I’ll get my own stuff.” Because I was tempted many times to go to work, heh-heh...
Take matters into your own hands, so to speak?

Go to work. One time Buhaina didn’t pay me. I said, “Buhaina, you’re a big rough guy, but you’re a junkie and I’m sober. All I got to do is wait for you to start nodding, and I’ll pull out my baseball bat...,” heh-heh-heh...
